text: Antipathy [Gr. anti , against, + paqoV , feeling]: Ger. Abneigung , Antipathie ; Fr. antipathie ; Ital. antipatia . A deep-seated and unreasoning mental aversion. See APPETENCE. Antipathy falls under the general history of IMPULSE (q.v.). It has reference to an object, generally an individual person, toward which the aversion is felt. Its unreasoning character is expressed often by the words 'unaccountable,' 'unreasonable,' 'instinctive,' and even 'physical' (when the physical signs of aversion are marked). As contrasted with aversion, it is intensive. It arises (1) through association of ideas (Spinoza), or (2) from inherited predisposition. ( J.M.B . - K.G .)
